newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-LATE KNOCKOUT BY WHITAKER SAVES DATE WITH DE LA HOYA.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-LATE KNOCKOUT BY WHITAKER SAVES DATE WITH DE LA HOYA.

text.p: Pernell Whitaker just barely saved his date with Oscar de la Hoya and his World Boxing Council welterweight title with an 11th-round knockout of Cuban-born U.S. resident Diobelis Hurtado Friday.

Trailing on all three scorecards after being knocked down twice, Whitaker unloaded a furious barrage of 10 unanswered blows that knocked Hurtado through the ropes and unconscious at 1:52 of the 11th round.

"It ain't over until we say it is over," said Whitaker, 40-1-1 with 17 victories inside the distance. "I knew it was going to happen. I knew I had to keep the pressure on him and it was just a matter of time before I really caught him."
Hurtado was taken to a local hospital for an examination after lying on the canvas at the Atlantic City Convention Centre Ballroom for several minutes.
"I didn't see it coming," Hurtado, who left Cuba to live in the United States two years ago, said of the knockout punches. "I got confused."
But until then, it was Hurtado who was confusing things with his unexpected stiff opposition opposition, as de la Hoya sat quietly at ringside.

Whitaker's arduous victory ensured that his April 12 fight with de la Hoya, considered the biggest bout in the division since Sugar Ray Leonard and Thomas Hearns battled more than 15 years ago, will go on.
"I couldn't look past Hurtado, I had to go through him to get to Oscar," said Whitaker.
Said de la Hoya: "Pernell is going to be the best that he can be and I'm going to be the best that I can be. And the best man is going to win."
The bout was only Hurtado's 21st as a pro and his first fight in the welterweight division. Whitaker was such a big favourite that there was no betting on the bout in Las Vegas casinos.

But Hurtado, 20-1, showed that he was not intimidated by his foe or by being in his first championship bout when he dropped Whitaker on the seat of his pants with the first punch of the fight, a straight right to the chin.
Hurtado caught Whitaker again in the sxith round, with a short chopping left to the chin that put the champion down a second time.
In the opening moments of the seventh round, Hurtado buckled Whitaker's knees with a straight right.

"He gave me all I could handle," Whitaker said of Hurtado, who lost a point for a low blow in the sixth round and for punching in the back of the head in the fifth. "He gave me my money's worth for a while.
"I can't take anything away from him. He came in here for my title with a champion's heart," Whitaker said.
